\begin{example} \end{example}[almost maximal diameter in dimension four]

Source: petersen:page-0312, petersen:page-0313 ↗ thm:pet-ch7-cheng-rigidity 1. ch7:7.2.6For $n=4$, consider metrics $dr^2+\rho ^2\sigma _1^2+\phi ^2(\sigma _2^2+\sigma _3^2)$ on $I\times S^3$, with \[ \rho (r)=\begin{cases} \dfrac {\sin (ar)}{a}& r\le r_0,\\ c_1\sin (r+\delta )& r\ge r_0,\end{cases}\qquad \phi (r)=\begin{cases} br^2+c& r\le r_0,\\ c_2\sin (r+\delta )& r\ge r_0,\end{cases} \] reflected in $r=\pi /2-\delta $ to produce a metric on $\mathbb {CP}^2\# \overline{\mathbb {CP}^2}$. For any small $r_0>0$ the parameters can be tuned so $\rho ,\phi $ are $C^1$ and generate a metric with $\Ric \ge 3$; as $r_0\to 0$ the parameter interval $I\to [0,\pi ]$, so the diameters converge to $\pi $, showing that subsection 2.2 does not admit a topological rigidity refinement when $n=4$. \end{example}
